h: Silent Prayer and the Cry From the Heart

p: In the Midrash Rabbah at the beginning of this parsha
pray in a loud voice?" etc.;
וְחַנָּה הִיא מְדַבֶּרֶת עַל לִבָּהּ (שְׁמוּאֵל א א, יג)
'And Channah, she spoke in her heart'" (Shmuel I 1:13).
And so they said, of blessed memory
"One who raises his voice in his prayer
is of those of little faith."
"'The voice is the voice of Yaakov' (Bereishis 27:22):
the voice of Torah and the voice of prayer";
and so we say in Shemoneh Esrei:
about the Men of the Great Assembly (Nechemiah 9:4):
"And they cried out with a loud voice."
that in ordinary prayer to Hashem Yisbarach
one should not raise his voice,
and that is of those of little faith;
when a person is in great distress
from the depth of the heart;
from the walls of his heart,
for he has no recourse at all;
as they said, of blessed memory
on "and they cried out with a loud voice,"
for they were in great distress
and there was no recourse to escape.
And prayer with a cry such as this
is accepted before Him, may He be blessed,
that one should not raise his voice,
שֶׁהוּא תְּפִלַּת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
which is the prayer of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
have had a cry in the heart
for which she was praying, for children;
is not commanded in pru u'rvu,
Therefore she spoke in her heart
the cry from the walls of her heart.
of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
although they said, of blessed memory
"Did he need to eat of its fruit?"
but rather he wanted to fulfill
the mitzvos that apply in the land
he was not obligated in this,
for the cry with the voice.
he was also not answered in his prayer.
that comes from the inwardness of the heart,
when he has no recourse to escape
And to this they alluded, of blessed memory,
on the pasuk "the voice is the voice of Yaakov":
two aspects of prayer are alluded to:
the first קֹל, without a vav,
and the second קוֹל, with the letter vav,
from the walls of the heart,
which draws down the vitality of salvation

p: in the Midrash Rabbah cited above
that they should pray in a time of trouble;
even though it was said to him
לֹא תַעֲבוֹר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן הַזֶּה (דְּבָרִים ג, כז)
כְּבָר לָמַדְנוּ מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
we already learned from Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
that one should vow and pray
"Hashem will answer you on the day of trouble;
the Name of the God of Yaakov will set you on high."
זֶה נִשְׁמָע מִיַּעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
this is learned from Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him:
that it should not come upon him, chas v'shalom.
אֲבָל מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם לָמַדְנוּ
But from Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him, we learn
which, as a person grasps it,
one should not hold himself back from praying;
with Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him:
even though it was said to him
כִּי לֹא תַעֲבוֹר אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּן הַזֶּה
"for you shall not cross this Jordan,"
And so it says in the Tanchuma
"Moshe taught all who come into the world
that a person should not say, etc.,
'and he has made a will,' etc.,
he stood aside and did not pray,
when Yeshayahu the prophet came to him
from the house of my father's father:
one should not hold himself back
Seemingly, why did he need to say
that he received this from his father's father?
Did we not learn this very thing
from Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him?
Even though it was said to him
וְאַף עַל פִּי כֵן הָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל
and all the more so Chizkiyah,
who heard only from the prophet!
אָמְנָם כִּי מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
However, from Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
only that a person is obligated to pray;
that his prayer will be accepted,
with Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
that he did not succeed with this prayer.
from the house of my father's father"
that is, from David HaMelech, peace be upon him,
that is, when the judgment has already been decreed
everything can be turned to good
and this is "one should not hold himself back
That is, in the episode of Bas Sheva,
when Nasan the prophet came to him
that is, he is the man
who pronounced the judgment upon himself;
and likewise the judgment went forth
שֶׁאֵין לוֹ שׁוּם תִּקְוָה חַס וְשָׁלוֹם
that he had no hope at all, chas v'shalom;
through his cry from the inwardness of the heart,
when he understood in his heart
that Hashem Yisbarach have mercy on him
to bring him out of his trouble,
even though he was not worthy;
as he said in his prayer (Tehillim 51:3):
"According to Your abundant mercy erase my transgressions," etc.;
לֵב טָהוֹר בְּרָא לִי אֱלֹהִים (שָׁם יב)
"Create in me a pure heart, O God" (there, 12);
and as they said, of blessed memory:
"This implies there is an impure one."
That is, when he thought in his heart,
that he saw that after all his toil
עַד שֶׁהָיָה לִבּוֹ חָלָל בְּקִרְבּוֹ (תְּהִלִּים קט, כב)
until "his heart was slain within him" (Tehillim 109:22),
as they said, of blessed memory,
that he killed the yetzer hara through fasting,
there was a great cry in his heart
except to create for him a new creation,
that he have a pure heart;
that Hashem Yisbarach had mercy on him
so that he became a new creation.
And this was what Chizkiyah received from him:
that one should not hold himself back
with the Men of the Great Assembly,
"And they cried out with a loud voice";
as they said, of blessed memory,
from the inwardness of the heart
for they understood in their hearts
the magnitude of the corruption and the distance
that resulted for them through it,
as they said, of blessed memory:
"This is the one that destroyed the Beis HaMikdash";
that Hashem Yisbarach abolish it from their hearts
and that they become a new creation;
for they said, "Neither them nor their reward,"
וְגַם עַל יֵצֶר הָרָע שֶׁל תַּאֲוָה
And they also asked about the yetzer hara of desire,
and it did not succeed in their hands,
because it is needed for the world;
for even in the time to come
it will not be entirely abolished,
but it will be called "Lavan," white,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק א קלז, א)
that one must be a mighty one
the greatness of its distance in this area,
from the inwardness of the heart to Hashem Yisbarach,
הוּא זוֹכֶה עַל יְדֵי רַחֲמֵי שָׁמַיִם
to become like a new creation,
